stem: A bar magnet of moment of inertia of 500 g cm\(^2\) makes 10 oscillations per minute in a horizontal plane. What is its magnetic moment, if the horizontal component of earth's magnetic field is 0.36 gauss?
solution:
Given: Moment of Inertia \(I = 500\) g cm\(^2\)
Frequency \(n = 10\) oscillation per minute \(= 10/60\) oscillations per second
Time period \(T = 6\) sec
\(B_{H} = 0.36\) gauss
From Eq. (11.8),
\(m = \dfrac{4\pi^2 I}{T^2 B}\)
\(m = \dfrac{4 \times (3.14)^2 \times 500 \times 10^{-7}}{36 \times 0.36 \times 10^{-4}}\)
\(m = 1.524\) A m\(^2\)

The region inside a current carrying toroid winding is filled with Aluminium having susceptibility \(\chi = 2.3 \times 10^{-5}\). What is the percentage increase in the magnetic field in the presence of Aluminium over that without it?
solution:
The magnetic field inside the solenoid without Aluminium \(B_{0} = \mu_{0} H\)
The magnetic field inside the solenoid with Aluminium \(B = \mu H\)
\(\dfrac{B - B_{0}}{B_{0}} = \dfrac{\mu - \mu_{0}}{\mu_{0}}\)
\(\mu = \mu_{0}(1 + \chi)\)
\(\dfrac{\mu}{\mu_{0}} - 1 = \chi\)
\(\dfrac{\mu - \mu_{0}}{\mu_{0}} = \chi\)
therefore \(\dfrac{B - B_{0}}{B_{0}} = \dfrac{\mu - \mu_{0}}{\mu_{0}} = \chi\)
Percentage increase in the magnetic field after inserting Aluminium is
\(\dfrac{B - B_{0}}{B_{0}} \times 100 = 2.3 \times 10^{-5} \times 100 = 0.0023\) %

stem: A domain in ferromagnetic iron is in the form of cube of side 1 \(\mu\)m. Estimate the number of iron atoms in the domain, maximum possible dipole moment and magnetisation of the domain. The molecular mass of iron is 55 g/mole and density is 7.9 g/cm\(^3\). Assume that each iron atom has a dipole moment of \(9.27 \times 10^{-24}\) Am\(^2\).
solution:
The volume of the cubic domain
\(V = (10^{-6})^3 = 10^{-18}\) m\(^3\) \(= 10^{-12}\) cm\(^3\)
mass \(=\) volume \(\times\) density \(= 7.9 \times 10^{-12}\) g.
An Avogadro number \((6.023 \times 10^{23})\) of iron atoms has mass 55 g.
The number of atoms in the domain \(N\)
\(N = \dfrac{7.9 \times 10^{-12} \times 6.023 \times 10^{23}}{55} = 8.651 \times 10^{10}\)
The maximum possible dipole moment \(m_{max}\) is achieved for the case when all the atomic moments are perfectly aligned (though this will not be possible in reality).
\(m_{max} = 8.65 \times 10^{10} \times 9.27 \times 10^{-24}\)
\(= 8.019 \times 10^{-13}\) Am\(^2\)
Magnetisation \(M = m_{max} /\) domain volume
\(= 8.019 \times 10^{5}\) Am\(^{-1}\)
